## 1. The man from the farthest part of the city  (`#the-man-from-the-farthest-part-of-the-city`)

Cited ayat: 36:20-27

> **36:20** وَجَآءَ مِنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
>
> **36:21** ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مَن لَّا يَسْـَٔلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ
>
> **36:22** وَمَا لِىَ لَآ أَعْبُدُ ٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنِى وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
>
> **36:23** ءَأَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ ءَالِهَةً إِن يُرِدْنِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ بِضُرٍّ لَّا تُغْنِ عَنِّى شَفَٰعَتُهُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يُنقِذُونِ
>
> **36:24** إِنِّىٓ إِذًا لَّفِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
>
> **36:25** إِنِّىٓ ءَامَنتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَٱسْمَعُونِ
>
> **36:26** قِيلَ ٱدْخُلِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يَٰلَيْتَ قَوْمِى يَعْلَمُونَ
>
> **36:27** بِمَا غَفَرَ لِى رَبِّى وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (36:20): A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, my people, follow the messengers.

**c2** (36:21): He told them to follow those who ask them for no payment and who are rightly guided.

**c3** (36:22-24): He asked why he should not worship the One who created him and to whom they will be returned, and asked whether he should take gods besides Him, when, if the Merciful wished him harm, their intercession would not avail him at all and they could not rescue him, for then he would be in clear error.

**c4** (36:25): He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him.

**c5** (36:26-27): He was told to enter the Garden, and he said that he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him and made him among the honoured.

### One-minute summary

A man came running from the farthest part of the city and told his people to follow the messengers [c1]. He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden, and he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him [c5].

### Complete story

A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said, my people, follow the messengers [c1]. He told them to follow those who ask them for no payment and who are rightly guided [c2]. He asked why he should not worship the One who created him and to whom they will be returned, and asked whether he should take gods besides Him, when, if the Merciful wished him harm, their intercession would not avail him at all and they could not rescue him, for then he would be in clear error [c3]. He said that he believed in their Lord and told them to listen to him [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden, and he said that he wished his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him and made him among the honoured [c5].

### Deep study

The ayat do not name the man, the city or the messengers [c1]. The ayah says that he was told to enter the Garden and does not say how or when he came to be there [c5].

### Kids mode

A man came running from the farthest part of the city [c1]. He told his people to follow the messengers [c1]. He said that he believed in their Lord [c4]. He was told to enter the Garden [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the man argues from his own worship of the One who created him [c3]. Another is that the passage ends with his wish that his people knew how his Lord had forgiven him [c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the man's name, his age or his work.
- Not established: the name of the city, or who the messengers were; the ayat before this passage speak of them.
- Not established: how he came to be told to enter the Garden, or what his people did.
- Not established: whether he is related to any other man described with similar words in another passage; nothing in the ayat links them.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: he is called Habib, and the city is identified in later works.
